text:
alex: Heads-up — us-central GPU pool at ~98% for the last 20m, 99th latency jumped, a few customers saw token stream stalls. We hit backpressure but our current per-tenant rate limits didn't stop a couple of bursty jobs. Thinking we need slot-accounting + lease revocations.

maria: link to grafana: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/cluster/gpu-usage?from=-30m :eyes: can you paste the query you used?

alex: query was `sum(avg_over_time(node_gpu_utilization[5m])) by (pool)` — i'll attach alerts screenshot in a sec.

kevin: I prototyped a slot-accounting model last week: each request consumes N "gpu-slots" based on batch-size and model type, leases are soft for T_soft=30s then hard for T_hard=300s. If a tenant exceeds its dynamic slot budget for >T_soft we start returning 429 with Retry-After and mark their leases as reclaimable.

kevin: snippet:
```
slot_policy:
  max_slots_per_tenant: 256
  slot_cost:
    llama-2-13b: 4
    quant-7b: 2
  soft_lease_seconds: 30
  hard_lease_seconds: 300
  reclaim_action: preempt_or_queue
```

hema: I like the idea but watch cache churn — if we preempt leases aggressively we evict KV caches and kill warm starts. Cost tradeoff: reclaiming might save GPU-minutes but add a huge token-regeneration penalty. We should differentiate stateful vs stateless workloads.

lia: Also consider regional locality: spilling heavy tenants to another region avoids immediate saturation but adds egress cost and latency. For EU customers we shouldn't auto-evict to us-east unless customer allows cross-region failover. Need an allowlist flag per account.

maria: can we compute tenant "burst score" from recent 5m P50/P95 req rates and recent commit level? We could combine commit (reserved capacity) and decay-weighted usage into a weight for fair allocation.

kevin: yes — propose weight = alpha * commit_weight + beta * recent_usage_score. Then slot budget = global_slots * weight / sum(weights). That handles committed customers.

alex: operational concerns: 1) we need fast path inside the scheduler to make per-request admission decisions with constant time. 2) telemetry to show per-tenant slot usage and reclaimed_count. 3) a fallback model variant (quantized) to route low-priority traffic instead of preempting.

opsbot: deploy-bot: Started rollout of `scheduler/slot-accounting` v0.3 to us-central (10 nodes) — canaries enabled.

sre-bot: ALERT: us-central pool GPU utilization > 95% (5m avg) — 1760312430 — All pods in pool are near capacity.

maria: quick sanity check — can someone run `./bin/slotctl tenant-usage --tenant=acme --window=5m` and paste output?

kevin: ran it for acme: `active_slots=78, soft_violations=3, hard_violations=0, reclaimed=1`

hema: proposal to reduce cache pain: introduce a "grace window" on cache eviction: reclaim compute but keep hot KV for 60s per-tenant with a soft eviction flag. If they come back before 60s we reassign warm slot without full re-warm. That costs memory but reduces regen tokens.

lia: +1. Also think about a small per-tenant LRU hotset that we persist on node-local SSD to accelerate rehydrate if full eviction occurs. Ops, what's the SSD spending impact?

alex: cost note: spilling 10% of heavy tenants to other region last week increased egress by ~$3.2k and reduced CPU/GPU overtime by 12%. Need to balance. For immediate mitigation we can try 429 with Retry-After + hint header telling SDK to backoff and optionally switch to cheaper model.

maria: SDK change: we can add a `x-redwood-retry-policy: slot_backoff;suggested_model=quant-7b` header when we emit 429 so client libs can transparently degrade. I'll open an SDK PR if we align on response format.

kevin: open questions: 1) exact slot cost math for multi-model pipelines, 2) what to show in Console UI for tenants (reclaimed count, current slots, weight), 3) safe defaults for soft/hard lease durations.

alex: next steps: kevin will land scheduler canary rules with soft-lease and reclaimable flag; maria will add Grafana panels; hema will draft cache-grace plan and SSD cost estimate; lia will sketch cross-region policy (opt-in/off). We'll reconvene in 1.5h or earlier if alerts fire.

maria: thanks, will prod the canary and report. :thumbsup:

kevin: started PR: https://github.com/redwood/scheduler/pull/842 — contains core slot accounting + metrics.

alex: nice. If canary shows >5% tail latency improvement for non-committed tenants without hurting committed customers, we ship to remaining us-central nodes.

sre-bot: RESOLVED ALERT: GPU utilization dropped to 83% after canary configs applied — 1760312479

lia: great work team. I'll follow-up on regional opt-in email content for enterprise customers.

alex: thanks everyone.
